claims.head: Iron sharpens iron
claims.body: The Panthers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Stars are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Panthers’ power play wins out. notes.text: Aleksander Barkov is on long-term injured reserve (knee injury) and has missed the last 19 games. He is one of their best players.
Brad Marchand is on injured reserve (knee injury) and has missed the last 17 games. He is a top-six forward.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 26% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Miro Heiskanen is day to day (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Tyler Myers has taken his spot beside Esa Lindell.
Lian Bichsel is out (lower body injury) and missed their last game. Esa Lindell has taken his spot beside Tyler Myers.
Matt Duchene has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Kyle Burroughs was added to the roster on Nov 15.

stakes: The Panthers go in fifth in the Atlantic with 26 points, the Stars fourth in the Central with 24 points.

story.head: Iron sharpens iron
paras: The Stars (11-6-2) beat Buffalo 2-0 last night, and the Panthers have won three straight. Going in, the Cats are fifth in the Atlantic (12th in the NHL) and the Stars fourth in the Central (14th).

This season, the Panthers have outscored teams 69-61, even though they’ve been outscored 41-36 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 22-15, and only one team creates more chances on the power play.

The Panthers are the league’s most physical team: first in forecheck pressure, first in physicality and first in rough stuff. As for the Stars, they block more shots than anyone (1st) and have a dangerous power play (1st). Dallas has allowed 2.47 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Panthers’ power play against the Stars’ penalty killers is strength against strength. Beyond that, both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Stars (lowest), so expect a tight one.

Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 25 A / 29 P in 21 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Sam Reinhart (12 G / 9 A / 21 P in 21 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for seventh in the NHL, with a point in six straight games against Dallas. For the Stars, Mikko Rantanen (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Jason Robertson (9 G / 11 A / 20 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind.
Akira Schmid (6-3-1 / .883 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to start for Florida, and Casey DeSmith (1-2-1 / .894 SV% in 4 GS) for Dallas.

items.text: Matthew Tkachuk is one point from 700.
The Panthers have been without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand for several games.
The Stars are newly without Lian Bichsel, have been without Miro Heiskanen since Nov 3, and have had to make do without Matt Duchene all season.
Wyatt Johnston has four goals on chances worth about 9.4 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
